clue.text: Caught a bird that's black or yellow

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the raven is a large all-black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher wonders whether the creature just netted is dark or golden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black or yellow' reads as a colour choice; 'yellow' is the definition, in its sense of cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means abjectly lacking courage.

clue.text: A blinding fall of water?

parts.note: a great waterfall, and also an eye condition clouding the lens that can blind

explanation.surface: A dazzling waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large waterfall and an opacity of the eye's lens causing blindness.

clue.text: A sequence was first put up in Sussex

parts.note: a run is a sequence, as of cards

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so the word for was first is read backwards

parts.note: led means was first, at the front

explanation.surface: A series that led the way was set up somewhere in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: ARUNDEL is a castle town in West Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic castle town found in the English county of Sussex.

clue.text: Plant hire a pub arranged nothing in it

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the rearranged letters, which the clue calls it
arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Hiring a bar for an arrangement of flowers with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges HIREAPUB, and 'nothing in it' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurge genus, a large group of plants with milky sap such as poinsettia.

clue.text: Some amphibians captured shortly without delay

indicators.note: the creatures named first hold the next word inside them, as captors hold a prisoner

parts.note: efts are newts, small amphibians
shortly means soon

explanation.surface: A naturalist reports that some newts were caught in short order.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word, as used by Spenser, for immediately or soon afterwards.

clue.text: Fugitive captain one of spirited courage?

definitions.text: Fugitive captain one of spirited courage?

parts.words: Fugitive captain one of spirited courage?
parts.note: the legendary ghost ship captain doomed to sail forever, and a play on spirited Dutch courage, the boldness from drink

explanation.surface: A runaway skipper who is brave from drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch courage is bravery from alcohol; 'spirited' means both ghostly and boozy.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary phantom ship and its captain, condemned to roam the seas, as in Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Like Philip as an appeal judge

definitions.text: Like Philip as an appeal judge

parts.words: Like Philip as an appeal judge
parts.note: the woman condemned by Philip of Macedon appealed from Philip drunk to Philip in his clear-headed state

explanation.surface: A man named Philip sitting as an appeal court judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'appeal from Philip drunk to Philip ...' comes from a woman who asked King Philip of Macedon to rehear her case once he had stopped drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Not drunk; the clear-headed Philip to whom the appeal was made.

clue.text: Surpass with gold in such sports

parts.note: to outdo is to surpass
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Beating rivals and taking gold in certain games.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air sports are those played outside rather than indoors.

clue.text: Dog ails terribly when out of this country

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stand outside the country, holding it
terribly signals the letters are badly mixed up

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is this country for a British paper

explanation.surface: A dog feels unwell when it is abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' is the anagram signal; 'out of' means outside, so the jumbled letters enclose the country. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender Middle Eastern hunting hound, the Persian greyhound.

clue.text: One helping to provide cast-off clothing?

definitions.text: One helping to provide cast-off clothing?

parts.words: One helping to provide cast-off clothing?
parts.note: in making a garment the last stitches are cast off, and this tool helps make the garment

explanation.surface: A charity helper who supplies second-hand clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast-off' suggests discarded clothes; in knitting, to cast off is to finish the stitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pointed rod used in pairs to make woolly garments.

clue.text: This honest fellow will never ring false

definitions.text: This honest fellow will never ring false

parts.words: This honest fellow will never ring false
parts.note: a genuine coin rings true when dropped on a counter, and an honest man is called by the old name for such a coin

explanation.surface: Praise for a trustworthy man who never sounds insincere.
explanation.walkthrough: The old test of a coin was to ring it on a counter; Shakespeare uses the word for an honest fellow (Hamlet calls the Ghost one).
explanation.definitionFit: An old term, used by Shakespeare, for a trusty, honest person, literally a genuine coin.

clue.text: Student pursuing exotic beast is a kind of nut

indicators.note: the student piece chases the beast piece, so it is written after it

parts.note: bête is French for beast, a foreign word for it
L is the learner driver's plate, a crossword student

explanation.surface: A learner is chasing some strange animal, and that animal is a type of nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' signals a foreign word: French bete, beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca palm's seed, chewed with leaf and lime across South Asia, is called this nut.

clue.text: Old soldier raced to ruin

indicators.note: to ruin the words is to wreck their order, so their letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone sped off to their own downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ruin' reads as purpose; 'to' is fodder and 'ruin' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantrymen of the past wore scarlet tunics and were nicknamed after them.

clue.text: Hence turkeys and not people

parts.note: nor means and not
folk means people

explanation.surface: A remark that turkeys, not humans, come from a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: NORFOLK is an English county in East Anglia famous for its turkeys; 'Hence' means from here.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Anglian county gives its name to a well-known breed of black turkey.

clue.text: Band of citizens drinking beer supplied by him

indicators.note: the band takes the beer into itself, just as a drinker swallows it

parts.note: CB stands for Citizens' Band radio
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A group of townsfolk drinking beer that one man has provided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is the definition: a man's name, Caleb, the biblical spy sent into Canaan.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, from the Old Testament spy, so it stands for some man.

clue.text: Points scored by Pakistani runner showing diligence

parts.note: a runner in crosswords is often a river; the Indus flows through Pakistan
a try scores points in rugby

explanation.surface: A Pakistani athlete earns points by working hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete but is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in the sense of hard work and steady application.

clue.text: Divination of a kind that is without a supporter

parts.note: sort means a kind

indicators.note: without means outside, so the short abbreviation goes around the supporter

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: A form of fortune-telling done with no backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Foretelling the future by drawing lots, a kind of fortune-telling.

clue.text: Rich once, constructing this coast road

indicators.note: constructing means the letters are built into something new

explanation.surface: Once wealthy, someone builds a seaside highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A road cut along a cliff or coast, as on the Riviera.

clue.text: Honest art is rejected in a sense

indicators.note: the turned word is placed within the sense word

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word art is read backwards

explanation.surface: Truthful art is turned down in a certain respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honest' is the definition; 'rejected' is the reversal signal and 'is' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means frank and upright, as in a straight answer.

clue.text: Metric measures set up for a bit of mosaic

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, 100 square metres
taken as written

explanation.surface: Metric measurements laid out for a piece of a mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ARES SET to give TES SERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square tile of stone or glass used in a mosaic.

clue.text: On which pirates aim to rule the waves …

definitions.text: On which pirates aim to rule the waves

parts.words: On which pirates aim to rule the waves
parts.note: pirate stations broadcast illegally, ruling the airwaves rather than the sea

explanation.surface: Buccaneers set out to control the oceans, echoing Rule, Britannia.
explanation.walkthrough: Offshore pirate broadcasters of the 1960s, such as Radio Caroline, transmitted from ships; 'waves' are airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The medium of broadcasting by airwaves, which unlicensed stations used from ships.

clue.text: Like an agent with authority placed in a document

indicators.note: placed in the document, so the one word sits within the other

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
put means placed

explanation.surface: An agent holding power named in a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputed means appointed to act for another, as an agent with delegated authority does.

clue.text: Island Byron's singer burned to leave?

definitions.text: Island Byron's singer burned to leave?

parts.words: Island Byron's singer burned to leave?
parts.note: Byron wrote of the isles of Greece where burning Sappho loved and sung; this was her island

explanation.surface: Byron's poet was so passionate she wanted off the island.
explanation.walkthrough: Byron's Don Juan: 'The isles of Greece... Where burning Sappho loved and sung'. Sappho came from this Aegean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island in the Aegean that was home to the poet Sappho.

clue.text: … but never thus to master us

definitions.text: but never thus to master us

parts.words: but never thus to master us
parts.note: Rule, Britannia says Britons never shall be slaves, so no one shall reduce them to bondage

explanation.surface: The patriotic song continues: no one will ever overpower us this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The song Rule, Britannia ends 'Britons never will be slaves'; the clue completes the line begun in 20 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To master someone by making them a slave is to put them in bondage.

clue.text: Moving a prison

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Relocating a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

clue.text: Bender that goes to a lady's head

definitions.text: Bender that goes to a lady's head

parts.words: Bender that goes to a lady's head
parts.note: a bent U-shaped clip worn in the hair, also a sharp bend in a road

explanation.surface: A drinking spree that leaves a woman tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bender' suggests a binge that goes to one's head; it is a bent wire clip worn in the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire pin used to hold a woman's hair in place.

clue.text: This goose found in London

explanation.surface: A particular wild goose has turned up in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: BRENT is a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dark wild goose is the brent; Brent is also a borough of north-west London.

clue.text: Form of speech heard, I see, in logical debate

parts.note: a dialect is a regional form of speech

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken and the letters written are what they sound like

parts.note: the words I see sound like the letters I and C

explanation.surface: A form of speech overheard during a reasoned argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the art of reasoning through argument and counter-argument.

clue.text: Leather has changed colour

indicators.note: changed means the letters of the short word are put in a new order

parts.note: green is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone's skin has turned a different hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns HAS into SHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough untanned hide, often of shark or ray, used for book covers and cases.

clue.text: Bumble's bugle perhaps, the French variety

parts.note: a bugle is a tube-shaped glass bead sewn on clothing
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Mr Bumble's horn, a French kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bumble is the beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist, so 'Bumble's' means his office. 'bugle' is a glass bead, not a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Bumble in Oliver Twist holds the post of parish officer, the job this word names.
